clue.text: Small private room near end of unit

parts.note: near means close, as in close to home

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word unit

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes a tiny room tucked away at the far end of a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small private room or cupboard, the sense in 'water closet' or a monarch's private chamber.

clue.text: Biscuits and nuts off one's trolley

definitions.meaning: off one's trolley is a British idiom for mad

explanation.surface: Biscuits and nuts tumble off a shopping trolley.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers are thin crisp biscuits, and as an adjective the word is British slang for crazy.

clue.text: Love some, but not all, abstract paintings

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a part is some but not all of something

explanation.surface: A viewer loves some abstract paintings but not all of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s style of abstract painting using optical illusions.

clue.text: Abu Dhabi, for example, angry after Middle East uprising

indicators.note: after puts the reversed letters before the word for angry
uprising in a down answer means the letters for Middle East are read upwards

parts.note: irate means angry

explanation.surface: News of anger following a Middle East uprising in Abu Dhabi.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the seven emirates of the UAE, a state ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Area in good order round university's central hall

indicators.note: round says the word for good order goes around the university letter

parts.note: being in good trim means being in good order
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A tidy campus space surrounds the university's main hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is the open central court or hall of a building.

clue.text: Traitor's initial motive for his crime?

definitions.text: Traitor's initial motive for his crime?

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of the word Traitor's

parts.note: a reason is a motive for doing something

explanation.surface: An investigator asks what first drove a traitor to his crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines: a traitor's crime is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the very offence that makes someone a traitor.

clue.text: Inn artist condemned on the way

indicators.note: condemned, like a ruined building, signals the letters of inn artist being broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A painter of inn signs is sentenced while being transported.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods in transit are being carried from one place to another, so they are on their way.

clue.text: Moving proposal

definitions.meaning: a formal proposal put to a meeting for a vote

explanation.definitionFit: Motion is movement, and a motion is also a proposal tabled for debate.

clue.text: Model soldier, like leader of mission

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
dig is slang for like, as in 'I dig that'

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word mission

explanation.surface: A model soldier is praised as fit to lead a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model soldier' reads as one phrase, but 'Model' is the definition and 'soldier' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a typical example or pattern to be copied, which is what a model is.

clue.text: Noel G's jam surprisingly includes R&B song

indicators.note: includes means the rearranged letters hold the pair inside them
surprisingly signals the letters of Noel G's jam turning up in an unexpected order

parts.note: R&B is rhythm and blues, written RB

explanation.surface: Noel Gallagher's jam session surprisingly features an R&B song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the jam letters into MOJANGLES; 'includes' slots R&B in after the M. 'R&B song' looks like the definition, but the song is only 'song'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Bojangles is a song by Jerry Jeff Walker, famously covered by Nina Simone and Sammy Davis Jr.

clue.text: Property in European country

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: Someone owns property in a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a piece of landed property, or all of a person's possessions.

clue.text: Sketch of Saint Christopher

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher

explanation.surface: An artist's sketch of Saint Christopher, patron of travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint Christopher' looks like one figure; split it into S and Kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch performed on stage.

clue.text: Diplomat dancing samba, pathetic otherwise

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of samba move about into a new order

parts.note: pathetic means sad, pitiful
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll be late'

explanation.surface: A diplomat who dances the samba but is otherwise hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a senior diplomat representing a country abroad.

clue.text: Diarist cross with Juliet wearing shades

parts.note: to bridge something is to cross it

indicators.note: wearing has the letter J sit inside the word for shades, as if dressed in it

parts.note: tones are shades of colour
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cross diary-writer, with Juliet in sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts J inside TONES to give TJONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget Jones is the fictional diarist of Helen Fielding's novel Bridget Jones's Diary.

clue.text: Loss of red mitten processed

indicators.note: processed means the letters of red mitten are worked over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A red mitten is lost in the wash, processed by machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment means harm or damage, a loss suffered by someone.

clue.text: Ordinary French wine I imported, rouge lacking body

indicators.note: imported means the letter I is brought into the wine's name

parts.note: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the Médoc region

indicators.note: lacking body leaves only the first and last letters of rouge

explanation.surface: An ordinary French wine is imported, a rouge with no body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking body' strips ROUGE to RE; 'imported' puts I in MEDOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means of only average or ordinary quality.

clue.text: Railway buff that's wizard on coaches

indicators.note: on places the wizard after the coaches in this across answer

parts.note: railway coaches coupled together make trains
Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J.K. Rowling's books

explanation.surface: A railway enthusiast who is a whizz on old coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wizard' looks like praise for the buff; it is Harry Potter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is a hobbyist who logs locomotive numbers, a classic railway enthusiast.

clue.text: Poison scare broadcast across Northern Ireland

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch over the pair, holding them inside
broadcast, scattered like seed, signals the letters of scare in a new order

explanation.surface: A poisoning scare is reported on air across Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles the scare letters into ARSEC; 'across' means that rearrangement spans the NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a toxic element, a classic poison of murder mysteries.

clue.text: Detailed decorative design around large dish

indicators.note: around means the shortened design goes round the letter for large
detailed is read as de-tailed, with the last letter cut off

parts.note: a pattern is a decorative design

explanation.surface: An intricately detailed pattern circles a large serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' cuts the tail N off PATTERN, leaving PATTER; 'around' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large flat serving dish.

clue.text: Belittle act, blue

parts.note: to do is to act
blue means sad or down

explanation.surface: Someone acts out sadness to make another feel small.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone down is to criticise or disparage them, making them seem lesser.

clue.text: Method of teaching singing, complicated solo in fact

indicators.note: complicated has the letters of solo in fact twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A method of teaching singing turns out to be a complicated solo.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa is a system naming notes doh, ray, me and so on, used to teach sight-singing.

clue.text: Run second leg

parts.note: pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

explanation.surface: An athlete runs the second leg of a relay.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short drive or run out, as in 'take the car for a spin'.

clue.text: Getting married in spring, so tighten one's belt

indicators.note: in means the letter for married goes inside the word for spring

parts.note: to skip is to spring or jump lightly

explanation.surface: A couple marrying in spring must economise to pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; it is SKIP, a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to spend or use as little as possible, economising like someone tightening their belt.

clue.text: Progressive kind joining Royal Navy

parts.note: a mode is a kind or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A forward-thinking, kindly person signs up for the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern thinking is up to date and forward-looking, as progressive views are.

clue.text: Article appears after group rehearsed play

indicators.note: appears after puts the article's word behind the group's word

parts.note: a set is a group of things
a piece is an article, as in a piece of furniture or writing

explanation.surface: A newspaper article follows a theatre group's rehearsed play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests A or THE; here it is PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a set piece is a pre-planned move practised in training, such as a corner routine.

clue.text: See literary review?

definitions.meaning: to see something is to spot or observe it
a review of a book in a newspaper, with the question mark marking the narrower sense

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks whether a literary review is worth a look.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or see, and a notice is a published review of a book or show.

clue.text: Nonsense written about Laurel originally having three parts

indicators.note: written about means the word for nonsense is set around the letter

parts.note: tripe is slang for rubbish or nonsense

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word Laurel

explanation.surface: Rubbish has been written about Laurel, perhaps of Laurel and Hardy, in a three-part piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple describes something made of three parts or members, as in a triple alliance.
